s: The characteristics features of genetic code are : i. It is always universal ii. It is triplet of nucleotides bases corresponding to 20 amino acids iii. It is non-overlapping, non-ambiguous and commaless. iv. It has start and stop codon Which of the statements given above are true?
x: The genetic code is the set of rules used by living cells to translate information encoded within genetic material (DNA or mRNA sequences of nucleotide triplets, or codons) into proteins. In other words, the genetic code may be defined as the exact sequence of DNA (or mRNA) nucleotides read as three letter words or codons, that determines the sequence of amino acids in protein synthesis. There are 64 codons which correspond to 20 amino acids and to signals for the initiation and termination of transcription. Each triplet (codon) specifies one amino acid in a protein structure or a start signal or stop signal in protein synthesis. With three exceptions, each codon encodes for one of the 20 amino acids used in the synthesis of proteins. There are 61 sense codons in the genetic code which code for 20 amino acids. Those codons that code for signals during protein synthesis are known as signal (start and stop) codons. There are four codons which code for signal. These are AUG (start codon), UAA, UAG and UGA (stop codons). AUG codon also codes for the amino acid methionine. Three non-sense or stop codons (UAA, UAG, UGA) do not code for amino acids but act as stop signals to terminate translation. The genetic code is always universal, commaless, non-overlapping, non-ambiguous and redundant.

Which one of the following techniques can be used to establish the paternity of a child?
x: DNA fingerprinting is a molecular technique used to identify individuals based on unique patterns in their DNA. Since a child inherits half of its genetic material from each parent, comparing the DNA profiles of the child and the alleged parent can accurately establish biological relationships such as paternity. Other techniques like protein analysis, chromosome counting, or quantitative DNA analysis do not provide the specificity and reliability required for paternity determination. Therefore, DNA fingerprinting is the most appropriate and widely used method for establishing paternity.

x: DNA fingerprinting is a powerful forensic technique used to establish an individual's identity and determine biological relationships such as paternity. It is widely used in criminal investigations, especially in rape and assault cases, as DNA can be extracted from trace biological samples. Evidence such as hair (with roots), saliva, blood, and dried semen contains genetic material sufficient for DNA profiling. Thus, the availability of DNA from such trace evidence explains why DNA fingerprinting is highly effective in establishing paternity and identifying criminals. s: The first crime ever solved using the DNA fingerprinting technique was in England in the year–

s: Which one of the following techniques can be used to establish the paternity of a child ?
x: DNA fingerprinting is used for paternity because polymorphisms are inherited, with the child getting half from each parent. Protein analysis, chromosome counting and quantitative DNA analysis lack this specificity.

s: The basis of DNA fingerprinting is :
x: DNA fingerprinting is a form of identification based on sequencing specific non-coding portions of DNA that are known to have a high degree of variability from person to person. Most of our DNA is identical to each other, but there are inherited regions of our DNA that can vary from person to person. These variations are termed as polymorphisms and this forms the basis of DNA fingerprinting. Since DNA from every tissue (skin, blood, saliva, bone, hair-follicle, sperm etc.) from an individual show the same degree of polymorphism, they become very useful identification tool in forensic applications. Further, as the polymorphisms are inheritable from parents to children, DNA fingerprinting is the basis of paternity testing.

x: DNA fingerprinting also called DNA typing, DNA profiling, genetic fingerprinting, genotyping or identity testing in genetics, is a method of isolating and identifying variable elements within the base-pair sequence of DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid). The technique was developed by British geneticist Alec Jeffreys after he noticed that certain sequences of highly variable DNA (known as minisatellites), which do not contribute to the functions of genes are repeated within genes. Jeffreys recognized that each individual has a unique pattern of mini-satellites (the only exceptions being multiple individuals from a single zygote, such as identical twins). DNA fingerprinting is a powerful tool to establish paternity and identity of criminals in rape and assault cases because DNA from trace evidence such as hairs, saliva and dried semen are adequate for DNA analysis.

x: The flavr-savr tomato was the first commercially grown genetically engineered food to be granted a license for human consumption. The novel variety was developed by insertion of an additional copy of the PG (Polygalacturonase) encoding gene in the “antisense” orientation, resulting in reduced translation of the endogenous PG messenger RNA (mRNA). x: Haemophilia is a genetic sex-linked disease in which blood clotting takes a long time in a patient (up to 24 hours) due to lack of thromboplastin protein in blood plasma. Women carry it while it appears in men (because men have one X-chromosome but women have two). It is also called bleeder’s disease which was first found in Queen Victoria. So it is also known as ‘royal haemophilia’ or ‘the royal disease’.

s: Which one of the following genetic disease is sex-linked?
x: Royal haemophilia is an X-linked (sex-linked) recessive disorder. Tay-Sachs and cystic fibrosis are autosomal, and hypertension is not a single-gene sex-linked disease.

s: Haemophilia is :
x: Haemophilia is an inherited genetic defect of blood clotting, not an infection caused by bacteria or viruses or by pollutants.

s: India's first genetically engineered vaccine is:
x: Shanvac-B, India's first genetically engineered vaccine, was developed against Hepatitis B Virus (HBV).

s: Which one of the following acids is present in sour milk products ?
x: Sour milk products such as curd contain lactic acid, formed by bacterial fermentation of lactose.

s: Milk openly placed for sometime becomes sour due to :
x: Milk contains a sugar called lactose. It also contains harmless bacteria called lactobacillus, which uses glucose for energy and creates lactic acid as a by-product. It is the lactic acid which makes the milk sour. The presence of lactic acid or lactate in milk is due to the fermentation of lactose caused mainly by lactic bacteria.

s: Which one of the following type of microorganisms is most widely used in industries ?
x: Bacteria, fungi and microalgae, all three are widely used in industries. Today bacteria is used in manufacturing curd, cheese, butter, vinegar and in making of various antibiotic medicines. Diatoms are a small group of algae. Diatomaceous soil consists of fossilized remains of diatoms, a type of hard-shelled algae. It is used in the manufacturing of glass and it is also used in sugarcane mills as bacteria filters. Fungus (yeast) have been used for thousands of years in the production of beer, wine and bread. Besides this different types of acids like citric acid, gallic acid etc. are also obtained from different types of fungus.

s: Vinegar is chemically known as :
x: Vinegar is chemically acetic acid (CH3COOH), made by Acetobacter.

s: A microbe commonly used for alcoholic fermentation in wine industry is a :
x: Yeasts have two main uses in food production :

s: The chemical name for vinegar is :
x: Vinegar is acetic acid, produced by Acetobacter. It is not an alcohol such as methanol or ethanol.

s: Which one of the following groups of organisms has significance in diagnosing the death by drowning?
x: Diatoms are useful in forensic studies. It has significance in diagnosing the death by drowning. Diatoms are photosynthetic algae and are found in almost every aquatic environment including fresh and marine waters, soils and almost at every humid place.

s: Yeast and mushrooms are :
x: Yeast and mushrooms are fungi because they lack chlorophyll. They are not algae, gymnosperms or roots.

s: An organism involved in the fermentation of toddy is :
x: Saccharomyces is a genus of fungi that include many species of yeasts. It is used in fermentation of toddy (a type of raw alcoholic beverage).

s: Which of the following converts milk into curd ?
x: Curd is formed when Lactobacillus bacteria convert lactose into lactic acid, souring and setting the milk. Vitamins and enzymes alone do not do this.

s: When milk is converted into curd, the sour taste is due to :
x: When milk is converted into curd, bacteria ferment lactose (the sugar present in milk), producing lactic acid. This lactic acid gives the curd its sour taste, which is clearly noticeable in curd.

s:
Which of the following statements is correct?
A. Sugarcane juice is fermented to form vinegar.
B. Vinegar has acetic acid.
C. Benzoic acid is the acid present in Vinegar.
D. Vinegar is used as a preservative.
Code :
x: Vinegar is made by Acetobacter fermentation (e.g. of sugarcane juice) and its acid is acetic acid, so A and B are correct. Benzoic acid is not the acid in vinegar, so C is wrong; D (preservative) is correct, giving A, B, D.

s: Which bacteria cause milk to spoil ?
x: Lactobacillus bacteria causes milk to spoil. It is a very important bacteria which is found in the intestinal tract. Lactobacillus uses lactose for energy and creates lactic acid as a by-product. It is the lactic acid which makes milk taste sour. It is used to make dairy products like cheese, curd etc. Apart from this, it is also used to control cholesterol.

s: Vinegar is the solution of which of the following?
x: Acetic acid (CH3COOH) or ethanoic acid is an organic acid, which is responsible for sour taste and the pungent smell of the vinegar. The physical and chemical properties prove that the vinegar is a solution of acetic acid. It is produced from fermentation of ethanol.

s: Which acid is found in Vinegar?
x: Acetic acid is the chief component of vinegar. Vinegar is a liquid consisting mainly of acetic acid (CH3COOH) and water. The acetic acid is produced by the fermentation of ethanol (formed from sugarcane juice and molasses) by acetic acid bacteria. It is mainly used as cooking ingredient and as a preservative.

s: Sour taste of vinegar is due to :
x: Vinegar's sour taste is due to acetic acid, which is not among tartaric, lactic or citric acid, so 'None of these' is correct.
